Secundus
see-KUN-dus
proper noun (figure)
Latin Secundus ("second"), a common Roman ordinal name, often given to a second child or borne by slaves and freedmen. A Thessalonian believer who accompanied Paul toward Jerusalem (Acts 20:4).

Biblical Definition

Secundus was a believer from Thessalonica who, with Aristarchus, represented the Thessalonian church among the delegates accompanying the Apostle Paul on his final journey toward Jerusalem with the relief collection: "And there accompanied him into Asia Sopater of Berea; and of the Thessalonians, Aristarchus and Secundus; and Gaius of Derbe, and Timotheus; and of Asia, Tychicus and Trophimus" (Acts 20:4). Of Secundus himself Scripture records only his name, his city, and his inclusion in this delegation; his Latin ordinal name ("second") suggests, like Quartus ("fourth") and Tertius ("third"), that he may have been a Roman of humble or servile background, identified by birth-order in the common manner of the servile classes. Yet he was chosen as one of the trusted men to represent his church in carrying the offering to Jerusalem — a real responsibility, for the collection was a substantial sum gathered from the Gentile churches for the poor saints in Judea, and Paul was careful that it be handled transparently by accountable delegates (2 Cor 8:18-21). Secundus thus stands among the named brethren of the collection — ordinary believers entrusted with a sacred stewardship, who traveled with the apostle through danger (Paul went up to Jerusalem knowing bonds and afflictions awaited him, Acts 20:23) to minister to the unity of the church. His name, like the names of Quartus, Tertius, Fortunatus, and Achaicus, is one of the many humble Roman names the Spirit preserved in Scripture — a quiet testimony that in Christ "there is neither Greek nor Jew... bond nor free: but Christ is all, and in all" (Col 3:11), and that the church was built, under God, by the faithful service of countless ordinary believers whose names the world would never have remembered but God did not forget.

Webster 1828 Definition

A Thessalonian believer who, with Aristarchus, accompanied Paul toward Jerusalem with the relief collection (Acts 20:4); his Latin name ("second") suggests humble origin; one of the named delegates entrusted with the sacred stewardship of the offering.

SECUNDUS, proper noun. Latin Secundus ("second"); a common Roman ordinal name, often of slaves and freedmen.

A believer of Thessalonica, named once: Acts 20:4, with Aristarchus.

One of the delegates accompanying Paul toward Jerusalem with the Gentile churches' relief collection.

His humble ordinal name (like Quartus, Tertius) suggests servile or humble origin.

One of the named brethren entrusted with the sacred stewardship of the offering (2 Cor 8:18-21).

Key Scripture

Acts 20:4 — "And there accompanied him into Asia Sopater of Berea; and of the Thessalonians, Aristarchus and Secundus; and Gaius of Derbe, and Timotheus; and of Asia, Tychicus and Trophimus."

Colossians 3:11 — "Where there is neither Greek nor Jew, circumcision nor uncircumcision, Barbarian, Scythian, bond nor free: but Christ is all, and in all."

Acts 20:22-23 — "And now, behold, I go bound in the spirit unto Jerusalem, not knowing the things that shall befall me there: Save that the Holy Ghost witnesseth in every city, saying that bonds and afflictions abide me."

2 Corinthians 8:19 — "And not that only, but who was also chosen of the churches to travel with us with this grace, which is administered by us to the glory of the same Lord."

Modern Corruption

Secundus is corrupted only when the obscure faithful are despised, when the named delegates of the collection are read as a mere travel list, or when the church forgets that it was built by the service of countless ordinary believers whose names God preserved.

expand to see more

Obscure-faithful despised. Secundus, like Quartus and Tertius, bears a humble Roman ordinal name and is known by a single mention. The world remembers the great; the Spirit of God preserved the names of these obscure servants. Secundus was trusted to represent his church and carry the sacred offering through danger to Jerusalem — a real stewardship. The church that learns from him learns that the body of Christ is built not chiefly by the famous few but by the faithful service of the many, whose names, unknown to the world, are written in heaven (Luke 10:20) and, for a few of them, preserved forever in the Word.

Secundus has no significant postmodern redefinition. The principal point worth recovering is the dignity of the obscure faithful and the model of accountable stewardship in the church's mercy ministry. Secundus was chosen by his church to travel with Paul and the collection (cf. 2 Cor 8:19) — a trust handled transparently. His humble name, preserved in Scripture, testifies that in Christ there is neither bond nor free (Col 3:11), and that God does not forget the service of the lowly.
